arab.seen: The constellation nearest the Pole: seven stars in the shape of a bear. Two of them, the Farqadan (the two calves), are two hand-spans apart. Just below the brighter one is a tiny, faint star the desert Arabs called Fa's al-Raha, "the axle of the millstone", around which the sky seems to turn. Above the bear's tail is al-Jady, the star by which the direction of prayer (the qibla) is found, because it hardly moves. The Arabs called the whole group Banat Na'sh al-Sughra, "the Lesser Daughters of Na'sh".

stories.title: The killing of Na'sh and the two guards
stories.text: A tale still told among the Bedouin says that al-Jady (the Pole Star) killed a man named Na'sh. His daughters lifted his body onto a bier and set out to take revenge. Four of them carry the bier and three walk behind, and they swore not to bury their father until his killer was dead. But two stars, the Farqadan, stand between them and al-Jady like guards, so the daughters circle him night after night and never reach him. That is why the Big Dipper turns forever around the Pole. (Other versions make Suhail the killer instead.)
stories.source: Popular Bedouin tradition, retold by Saudi and Gulf sky-watchers

stories.title: The guide of travellers
stories.text: Because al-Jady barely moves, it was the Arabs' compass. Ibn Qutayba says the qibla is found by it, and quotes the poet al-Ra'i about camels crossing the desert at night: "When they climb onto a waterless waste, they take no guide but the whiteness of the two Farqads."
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: Nearest of them to the Pole, know this, are stars arranged in the figure of a bear.

a: رسّمن و القطب معاً في بقعة
full.e: When you count them they are seven, drawn together with the Pole in one patch of sky.
Within the whole figure are two stars, two hand-spans apart;
the Bedouins named them the two Farqads; and just below the brighter of the two you see
a tiny star, fainter than a fading trace, which the desert Arabs call 'the axle of the millstone'.

a: نعم و نجم تعرف القبلة به
full.e: Yes, and there is a star by which the qibla is known; it sits just above the bear's tail.
The Arabs know it as al-Jady; its circle runs close to the Pole.
The Arabs call the stars of this bear the Daughters of Na'sh: so the books tell.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 8 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: أقرب الصور إلى القطب: سبعة كواكب على صورة دبّ. منها الفرقدان وبينهما شبران، وتحت أنورهما كويكب خفيّ تسمّيه الأعراب فأس الرحى لأن السماء تدور حوله كما تدور الرحى. وفوق ذنب الدب الجَدي الذي تُعرف به القبلة لأنه لا يكاد يتحرك. وتسمّي العرب نجوم هذه الصورة بنات نعش الصغرى.

stories.title: مقتل نعش والحارسان
stories.text: تحكي الحكاية المتداولة عند أهل البادية أن الجدي قتل رجلًا اسمه نعش، فحملته بناته على نعشه وخرجن يطلبن الثأر: أربع يحملن النعش وثلاث يمشين خلفه، وأقسمن ألّا يدفنّ أباهن حتى يقتلن قاتله. لكن الفرقدين يقفان بينهن وبين الجدي كالحارسين، فيظللن يدرن حوله كل ليلة ولا يصلن إليه أبدًا، ولذلك تدور بنات نعش حول القطب إلى الأبد. وفي روايات أخرى القاتل هو سهيل.

stories.title: دليل المسافرين
stories.text: لأن الجدي لا يكاد يتحرك كان بوصلة العرب. يقول ابن قتيبة: به تُعرف القبلة وبه يقع الاستدلال، ويستشهد بقول الراعي في الإبل تقطع الصحراء ليلًا: «لا يتّخذن إذا علون مفازةً ... إلا بياضَ الفرقدين دليلا».

greek.seen: A small bear: Arcas, or one of the nymphs who nursed the baby Zeus.

stories.title: The son who became a bear
stories.text: In one version, Arcas, son of the nymph Callisto, was hunting when he met a great brown bear. It was his own mother, whom Zeus had transformed. To keep him from killing her, Zeus turned Arcas into a bear too and set them both in the sky, the son close beside the mother, watching over her for ever. Another tradition says the Little Bear is Cynosura, one of the nymphs of Mount Ida who hid the infant Zeus from his father Cronus. Greek sailors from Phoenicia steered by the Little Bear, which stays close to the Pole.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: دبّ صغير: أركاس، أو إحدى الحوريات اللواتي أرضعن زيوس الطفل.

stories.title: الابن الذي صار دبًّا
stories.text: في إحدى الروايات، كان أركاس ابن الحورية كاليستو يصطاد حين لقي دبًّا بنيًّا كبيرًا، وكانت هي أمّه التي مسخها زيوس. فلكي لا يقتلها، حوّل زيوس أركاس أيضًا إلى دبّ ورفعهما إلى السماء، الابن قريبًا من أمه يرعاها إلى الأبد. وتقول رواية أخرى إن الدب الأصغر هو كينوسورا، إحدى حوريات جبل إيدا اللواتي أخفين الطفل زيوس عن أبيه كرونوس. وكان بحّارة الإغريق القادمون من فينيقيا يهتدون بالدب الأصغر لقربه من القطب.

egypt.seen: Part of the hippopotamus goddess and the 'imperishable' stars.

stories.title: The stars that never die
stories.text: The Egyptians called the stars that circle the Pole without setting the 'imperishable ones'. The narrow shafts of the Great Pyramid seem to point toward this northern region, where the dead king was meant to join the stars for ever. The hippopotamus goddess Taweret was pictured here, holding the bull's foreleg of Set in place.
stories.source: Egyptian Streets, 'Ancient Egyptian constellations' (2024); Pyramid Texts

ar.seen: جزء من إلهة فرس النهر ومن «النجوم التي لا تفنى».

stories.title: النجوم التي لا تموت
stories.text: سمّى المصريون النجوم التي تدور حول القطب دون أن تغيب «التي لا تفنى». وتبدو الممرات الضيّقة في الهرم الأكبر كأنها تشير إلى هذه الناحية الشمالية، حيث كان الملك الميت سيلحق بالنجوم إلى الأبد. وصُوّرت هنا إلهة فرس النهر تاورت ممسكة بساق ثور ست في مكانها.

china.seen: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure, palace of the Celestial Emperor.

stories.title: The emperor at the centre
stories.text: The stars around the North Pole formed Ziwei Yuan, the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, the palace of the Celestial Emperor, surrounded by walls of stars, ministers, consorts and guards. The earthly emperor's palace in Beijing, the Forbidden City, was named after it. Just as the stars turn around the Pole, the empire was meant to turn around its ruler. Confucius said: 'Ruling by virtue is like the Pole Star, which stays in its place while all the stars pay homage to it.'
stories.source: Confucius, Analects 2.1; Shiji

ar.seen: الحرم الأرجواني المحظور، قصر الإمبراطور السماوي.

stories.title: الإمبراطور في المركز
stories.text: كانت النجوم حول القطب الشمالي «زيوي يوان» أي الحرم الأرجواني المحظور، قصر الإمبراطور السماوي تحيط به أسوار من النجوم ووزراء وزوجات وحرّاس. وسُمّي قصر الإمبراطور في بكين «المدينة المحرّمة» باسمه. وكما تدور النجوم حول القطب كان على الإمبراطورية أن تدور حول حاكمها. قال كونفوشيوس: «الحكم بالفضيلة كنجم القطب، يبقى في مكانه وتتوجّه إليه النجوم كلها».

india.seen: Dhruva, the boy who became the Pole Star.

stories.title: The unmoving boy
stories.text: Dhruva was a young prince whose father, King Uttanapada, preferred his other son. When his stepmother told him he could never sit on his father's lap, five-year-old Dhruva went into the forest to pray to the god Vishnu. He meditated with such determination, standing on one foot and barely breathing, that the gods themselves were shaken. Vishnu appeared and granted him a place above all the worlds, fixed and unmoving: the Pole Star, around which the seven sages turn.
stories.source: Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana

ar.seen: دروفا، الصبي الذي صار نجم القطب.

stories.title: الصبي الثابت
stories.text: كان دروفا أميرًا صغيرًا يفضّل أبوه الملك أوتانابادا ابنه الآخر عليه. فلمّا قالت له زوجة أبيه إنه لن يجلس في حجر أبيه أبدًا ذهب الطفل ذو السنوات الخمس إلى الغابة يدعو الإله فيشنو، وتأمّل بعزم شديد واقفًا على قدم واحدة لا يكاد يتنفّس حتى اهتزّت الآلهة نفسها. فظهر له فيشنو ومنحه مكانًا فوق العوالم كلها ثابتًا لا يتحرك: نجم القطب الذي يدور حوله الحكماء السبعة.

arab.seen: The Great Bear, which the Greeks called the greatest bear. Four stars in a square turn around the Pole "like a waterwheel". The Arabs called them al-Na'sh, the bier, and the three stars that follow are al-Banat, the daughters. The poet names the stars one by one: al-Jawn, 'Anaq, and the tiny al-Suha, which was used to test eyesight, and finally al-Qa'id, "the leader". Below the bear are three pairs of stars called al-Qafazat, the gazelle's leaps. Near them are the faint Gazelles themselves and an empty patch of sky called al-Hawd, the pool. A star near the Lion is called Kabid al-Asad, "the Lion's liver".

stories.title: The Daughters of Na'sh
stories.text: The four stars of the bowl are the bier of the murdered Na'sh, and the three stars of the handle are his daughters walking behind it. The first daughter is called al-Qa'id (the leader), the middle one 'Anaq, and the one nearest the bier al-Jawn. Beside the middle daughter is a star so small it almost touches her: al-Suha.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

stories.title: "I show her al-Suha, and she shows me the moon"
stories.text: The Arabs tested their eyes on al-Suha: whoever couldn't see it had weak sight. This became a proverb, "Uriha al-Suha wa turini al-qamar". Someone points out the faint, hidden star, and the other person answers by pointing at the huge, obvious moon. It is said of a person who replies to something subtle with something everybody already knows.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); the Urjuza itself

stories.title: The Lion's tail and the gazelles' leaps
stories.text: The Arabs said: "The Lion struck the ground with its tail, and the gazelles leapt." The tail-tuft of the great Arab Lion (al-Hulba, the stars of Coma Berenices) lies near the Bear. When it lashed the ground, the gazelles bolted in three great bounds and left three pairs of hoof-prints in the sky, al-Qafazat. Once they were safe, they came down to drink at al-Hawd, the pool: an empty, starless patch of sky. The faint stars nearby are the gazelles themselves and their young.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); al-Marzuqi, al-Azmina wa al-Amkina (11th c.); Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib)

full.e: And near it are many stars, their bodies bright and shining;
the Greeks named them the Greatest Bear, likening it to the one before.
Within the bear are four stars, shaped into a square;
they turn around the Pole like a waterwheel; the Bedouins know them as 'the Bier'.
You see them showing at every hour; the desert people named them the Bier.
Three stars follow them in a row, gleaming to the eye when night grows dark;
facing the stars of the wild beasts, they are called the Sons of Na'sh and the Family of Na'sh,
and the Arabs named them the Daughters, and the tongues of the reporters agree
that the one of these three that comes nearest the square
is known among the Bedouins as al-Jawn: so it is told by men of learning.
Then the star that follows this one is a dazzling star whose name
among the Bedouins is 'Anaq, know it; and just above it is a small, dim star
which some Bedouins called al-Suha, and some reports give it as al-Suta;
a group who have some link to star-lore call it Nu'aysh,
and another group knows it as al-Saydaq; and it has come from a trustworthy man of experience
that by it eyesight is put to the test, and about it there runs a well-known proverb:

a: قول الذي قال أُري هذا السها
full.e: the saying of one who said: 'I show him al-Suha, and he shows me the full moon', out of ignorance and blindness.
After this star comes a single star, brilliant, full of light, called al-Qa'id, the Leader.
Beneath the stars of the Bier and the Daughters are stars known as al-Qafazat, the Leaps;
they lie at the edges of this bear, close to the Daughters and al-Suha.
A reporter from the Bedouins, who does not lie, has also called them al-Qara'in, the Pairs,
and they may be called al-Nawafiz, the Bounders: they are the tracks of the leaping gazelles.
'The little cows' is a name for those lights, and the Arabs also call them al-Qumayzat;
and with most of the reporters they are also known as al-Thu'aylibat, the little foxes.
Before them go small stars, many of them, forming no figure,
hidden, utterly faint: the Bedouins know them as the Gazelles.
Above them is a small round patch of sky, following the Bier,
empty, holding not a single star: the scholars call it al-Hawd, the Pool.
The ancients told that the gazelles one day took fright
at the figure of the Lion close by the stars of the Bear we have described,
and in their fear they leapt away, and so won their share of safety;
then they came down to the Pool, safe, escaped from the harm of the forest-lion,
and their tracks remained upon the ground: those Leaps are the gazelles' tracks.
And after the figure comes a shining star that you see flickering in the dark of night;
the Bedouins make it the Lion's liver, because it lies close to the shape of the Lion.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 35 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: الدب الأكبر عند الروم. أربعة كواكب مربّعة تدور حول القطب «كالدولاب» تسمّيها العرب النعش، والثلاثة التي تتبعها البنات. ويسمّي الناظم كواكبها واحدًا واحدًا: الجَون والعناق والسُّها الخفيّ الذي تُمتحن به الأبصار، ثم القائد. وتحت الدب ثلاثة أزواج من الكواكب هي القفزات، وبقربها الظباء، وبقعة خالية من النجوم تسمّى الحوض، ونجم قرب الأسد يسمّى كبد الأسد.

stories.title: بنات نعش
stories.text: الأربعة التي في المربّع نعشُ نعشٍ المقتول، والثلاثة التي في الذيل بناته يمشين خلفه. أولى البنات القائد، والوسطى العَناق، والتي تلي النعش الجَون. وإلى جانب الوسطى كوكب صغير جدًا يكاد يلزق بها هو السُّها.

stories.title: «أُريها السُّها وتُريني القمر»
stories.text: كانت العرب تمتحن أبصارها بالسُّها، فمن لم يره فقد ضعف بصره. ومنه المثل: «أُريها السُّها وتُريني القمر»: تُشير إلى النجم الخفيّ الدقيق، فيُشار لك إلى القمر الظاهر لكل أحد. يُضرب لمن يُجيب عن الأمر الدقيق بالأمر المعروف الواضح.

stories.title: ذيل الأسد وقفزات الظباء
stories.text: تقول العرب: «ضرب الأسدُ بذنبه الأرضَ فقفزت الظباء». فلمّا ضرب الأسد العظيم الأرض بهُلبته (نجوم الضفيرة) نفرت الظباء ووثبت ثلاث وثبات، فتركت في السماء ثلاثة آثار من أظلافها هي القفزات. ولمّا أمنت وردت الحوض، وهو بقعة خالية من النجوم. والنجوم الخفية حولها هي الظباء وأولادها.

greek.seen: The Great Bear, Callisto; also called the Wagon (Hamaxa).

stories.title: Callisto
stories.text: Callisto was a huntress in the company of Artemis, sworn never to marry. Zeus fell in love with her, and when Hera discovered it she turned Callisto into a bear (in other versions Zeus or Artemis did it). Years later her son Arcas almost speared the bear while hunting. Zeus snatched them both up into the sky. Hera, still angry, asked the sea-gods Oceanus and Tethys never to let the bear bathe in their waters, which is why the Great Bear never sets below the horizon in Greece.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Ovid, Metamorphoses 2

poem.orig:
Ἄρκτον θ᾽, ἣν καὶ Ἄμαξαν ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν,
ἥ τ᾽ αὐτοῦ στρέφεται καί τ᾽ Ὠρίωνα δοκεύει,
οἴη δ᾽ ἄμμορός ἐστι λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο.
poem.trans:
…and the Bear, which people also call the Wagon,
which turns in its place and keeps watch on Orion,
and alone has no share in the baths of Ocean.
poem.by: Homer, Iliad 18.487–489 (the stars on Achilles' shield)

ar.seen: الدب الأكبر، كاليستو، ويسمّى أيضًا العربة.

stories.title: كاليستو
stories.text: كانت كاليستو صيّادة في صحبة أرتميس أقسمت ألّا تتزوّج. فأحبّها زيوس، ولمّا علمت هيرا مسختها دبّة (وفي روايات أخرى زيوس أو أرتميس هو الذي فعل). وبعد سنين كاد ابنها أركاس يطعن الدبّة برمحه وهو يصطاد، فاختطفهما زيوس إلى السماء. وظلّت هيرا غاضبة، فطلبت من إلهي البحر أوقيانوس وتيثيس ألّا يسمحا للدبّة بالاستحمام في مياههما أبدًا، ولذلك لا يغيب الدب الأكبر تحت الأفق في بلاد الإغريق.

egypt.seen: Meskhetiu, the foreleg of a bull; or an ox ploughing the earth.

stories.title: The thigh of Set
stories.text: The seven stars of the Big Dipper were Meskhetiu, the foreleg of a bull, linked to the god Set, the murderer of his brother Osiris. They were also seen as an ox ploughing the earth, connected to the great battle between Set and Horus. Because these stars never set, they belonged to the 'imperishable stars' of the north, where the souls of kings hoped to go. An adze shaped like this foreleg was used in the 'opening of the mouth' ceremony that brought a mummy back to life.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Wikipedia, 'Meskhetyu'

ar.seen: مسخيتيو، أي ساق ثور أمامية، أو ثور يحرث الأرض.

stories.title: فخذ ست
stories.text: كانت النجوم السبعة في المغرفة «مسخيتيو» أي الساق الأمامية لثور، وارتبطت بالإله ست قاتل أخيه أوزيريس. ورآها المصريون أيضًا ثورًا يحرث الأرض، وربطوها بالمعركة الكبرى بين ست وحورس. ولأن هذه النجوم لا تغيب كانت من «النجوم التي لا تفنى» في الشمال، حيث كانت أرواح الملوك ترجو أن تذهب. وكانت قَدُوم على شكل هذه الساق تُستعمل في طقس «فتح الفم» الذي يعيد الحياة إلى المومياء.

china.seen: Beidou, the Northern Dipper: the chariot of the Celestial Emperor.

stories.title: The dipper that tells the seasons
stories.text: The seven stars were Beidou, the Northern Ladle. It was imagined as the carriage of the Celestial Emperor, who rides around the Pole. In the evening its handle points east in spring, south in summer, west in autumn and north in winter, so it was used as a calendar. The Chinese also saw it as a small wagon with two people running behind.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Sima Qian, Shiji, 'Book of the Celestial Offices'

stories.title: Life and death in the two dippers
stories.text: In a story from the 4th-century Soushen ji, the fortune-teller Guan Lu met a young man fated to die at nineteen. He told him to bring wine and dried meat to two old men playing a board game under a mulberry tree. The men ate and drank without noticing him, and when they finally saw him, they could not refuse his request. One of them changed '19' in his book to '99'. Guan Lu explained: the man in the south was the Southern Dipper, who records births, and the man in the north was the Northern Dipper, who records deaths.
stories.source: Gan Bao, Soushen ji

ar.seen: بيدو، المغرفة الشمالية: عربة الإمبراطور السماوي.

stories.title: المغرفة التي تخبر بالفصول
stories.text: كانت النجوم السبعة «بيدو» أي المغرفة الشمالية، وتُخيّلت عربة الإمبراطور السماوي يدور بها حول القطب. وفي المساء يشير ذيلها إلى الشرق في الربيع، وإلى الجنوب في الصيف، وإلى الغرب في الخريف، وإلى الشمال في الشتاء، فكانت تقويمًا. ورآها الصينيون أيضًا عربة صغيرة يجري خلفها شخصان.

stories.title: الحياة والموت في المغرفتين
stories.text: في حكاية من كتاب «سوشن جي» في القرن الرابع، لقي العرّاف قوان لو شابًا مقدّرًا له أن يموت في التاسعة عشرة، فأمره أن يحمل خمرًا ولحمًا مجففًا إلى شيخين يلعبان لعبة لوحية تحت شجرة توت. فأكل الشيخان وشربا دون أن ينتبها إليه، فلمّا رأياه لم يستطيعا ردّ طلبه، فغيّر أحدهما «19» في كتابه إلى «99». وشرح قوان لو: الشيخ الذي في الجنوب هو المغرفة الجنوبية التي تسجّل المواليد، والذي في الشمال هو المغرفة الشمالية التي تسجّل الوفيات.

japan.seen: Hokuto Shichisei, the Seven Stars of the North Dipper.

stories.title: The seven stars of the north
stories.text: The Big Dipper was Hokuto Shichisei, the 'seven stars of the northern dipper', taken from China and honoured in Buddhist and Taoist rituals for long life and protection. Sailors and farmers used it to find north and to tell the time at night.
stories.source: Traditional; Japanese star folklore collected by Nojiri Hōei

ar.seen: هوكوتو شيتشيسي، النجوم السبعة للمغرفة الشمالية.

stories.title: نجوم الشمال السبعة
stories.text: كانت المغرفة «هوكوتو شيتشيسي» أي «النجوم السبعة للمغرفة الشمالية»، أُخذت عن الصين وكُرّمت في طقوس بوذية وطاوية لطول العمر والحماية. واستعملها البحّارة والفلاحون لمعرفة الشمال والوقت ليلًا.

india.seen: Saptarishi, the Seven Sages, with Arundhati.

stories.title: The seven sages and the faithful wife
stories.text: The seven stars of the Big Dipper are the Saptarishi, seven great sages who receive the sacred knowledge of the Vedas in each age of the world. Next to Vasishtha (Mizar) is a tiny star, Arundhati (Alcor), his devoted wife. In Hindu weddings the bride and groom are still shown Arundhati as a model of faithful married love. In a story from the Mahabharata, the wives of six of the sages were the Krittikas (the Pleiades), while Arundhati alone stayed beside her husband.
stories.source: Mahabharata; Wikipedia, 'Saptarishi'

poem.orig:
अमी य ऋक्षा निहितास उच्चा
नक्तं ददृश्रे कुह चिद्दिवेयुः
poem.trans:
Those Bears placed high above, seen at night,
where do they go by day?
poem.by: Rig Veda 1.24.10

ar.seen: سابتاريشي، الحكماء السبعة، ومعهم أروندهاتي.

stories.title: الحكماء السبعة والزوجة الوفيّة
stories.text: النجوم السبعة في المغرفة هي «سابتاريشي»، سبعة حكماء عظام يتلقّون معرفة الفيدا المقدّسة في كل عصر من عصور العالم. وبجانب فاسيشتا (العناق) نجم صغير جدًا هو أروندهاتي (السُّها) زوجته المخلصة، وما زال العروسان في الأعراس الهندوسية يُريان أروندهاتي مثالًا للحب الزوجي الوفيّ. وفي حكاية من المهابهاراتا كانت زوجات ستة من الحكماء هنّ الكريتيكا (الثريا)، وبقيت أروندهاتي وحدها بجانب زوجها.

arab.seen: The Dragon curls around the polar circle. The Arabs did not see a dragon here. They saw a desert scene. Four bright stars in its head are the 'Awa'idh, mother camels, gathered around a faint star, al-Rub', the young camel born in spring. A star called the Wolf covets the calf, but the mothers and the Eagle protect it. There are also al-Athafi (the three hearth-stones), the wolf's claws, a second wolf (the pair is called al-Dhi'ban, also al-Hurran or al-'Awhaqan), and a bright star called al-Dhikh, the male hyena, which is also hungry for the calf.

stories.title: The mother camels and the calf
stories.text: Ibn Qutayba describes four stars in an uneven square with a faint, smudge-like star in the middle, and says they were "likened to little she-camels bending over a young calf". The calf, al-Rub', is a camel born early in the spring. Nearby, two wolves (al-Dhi'ban) creep in from the direction of the Pole Stars, with their claws (Azfar al-Dhi'b) out in front of them. A red male hyena (al-Dhikh) and a crowd of hyenas and cubs lurk further off. The mothers close their ring, and the calf is never taken. Several modern star names come from this scene: Alwaid, Dziban and Alrakis.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib)

full.e: After it come the stars of the Dragon, explained by one of steady speech.
The stars of the Dragon curl like a heart around the circle of the Pole.
The first of them is a star of hidden light, without brightness or size;

a: و هو على لسان رأس الايم
full.e: it is known as al-Raqis, the Dancer, among the people, and it sits on the tongue of the serpent's head.
It is followed by stars gathered together, four in number if you count them,
surrounding a faint star that only a sharp-eyed person can see;
the scholars know it as al-Rub', the young camel, and al-Rifd was also heard from them as its name.
Those four great stars (so reports have reached us)
the Arabs imagine as mother camels, and the little calf as sheltering among them
for fear of a star they named the Wolf, which you see close beside it.

a: و ليس في استيلائه من طمع
full.e: They say it covets the young camel, but there is no hope of its seizing him,
for those bright stars drive off the danger from him with all their strength,
and the Eagle too leans over him in pity, so the wolf can never reach him.
They are followed by three hidden stars, neither bright nor shining,
like daisies about to wither: the Bedouins know them as al-Athafi, the hearth-stones.
After them come two dim stars, both close to them;
they are the claws of the Wolf, they say; so the reports from them tell,

a: و الذيب نجم قد ذكرنا خبره
full.e: and the Wolf is the star whose story we have told, as if the claws were following its tracks.
After this wolf there is another wolf, its body close to the first one's body;
the Arabs named both stars, know it, the Two Wolves and the Two Whelps;
the Bedouins named them the Two Wolves, and they may be called the Two Male Bustards,

a: عن كل ذي علم يفيض فيضا
full.e: and 'the Two Black Swallows' we have also heard, from every scholar who overflows with learning.
They are followed by a star of plentiful light, shining for the watcher in the darkness;
the Bedouins know it as al-Dhikh, the male hyena; you see it near the wolves,

a: و هو مع الذيبين مغرى بالربع
full.e: and sometimes it is called the Hyena; it too, with the two wolves, is eager for the calf.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 25 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: التنين يلتفّ حول دائرة القطب. ولم ترَ العرب هنا تنينًا بل مشهدًا من البادية: أربعة كواكب نيّرة في رأسه هي العوائذ، أي النوق الأمّهات، حول كوكب خفيّ هو الرُّبَع، أي الفصيل المولود في الربيع. ونجم يسمّى الذئب يطمع فيه، لكن الأمهات والنسر يحمينه. وفيها الأثافي وأظفار الذئب والذئبان (ويسمّيان الحَرّين والعوهقين)، وكوكب نيّر هو الذِّيخ، أي ذكر الضباع، وهو أيضًا طامع في الفصيل.

stories.title: النوق والفصيل
stories.text: يصف ابن قتيبة أربعة كواكب على تربيع مختلف وفي وسطها نجم كاللطخة، ويقول: «شُبِّهن بأُنَيقٍ عطفن على رُبَع». والرُّبَع ولد الناقة في أول النتاج. وبالقرب منه ذئبان يقبلان من جهة الفرقدين وأمامهما أظفارهما، وذِيخٌ أحمر وضباع وأولادها تتربّص في الجوار، والنوق تضمّ حلقتها فلا يُؤخذ الفصيل أبدًا. ومن هذا المشهد جاءت أسماء نجوم حديثة مثل Alwaid (العوائذ) وDziban (الذئبان) وAlrakis (الراقص).

greek.seen: A serpent-dragon: Ladon, guardian of the golden apples.

stories.title: The dragon of the Hesperides
stories.text: Ladon was the never-sleeping serpent coiled around the tree of golden apples in the garden of the Hesperides, at the western edge of the world. Hera had planted the tree, a wedding gift from the Earth. For his eleventh labour Heracles had to bring back the apples, and in many versions he killed Ladon to get them. Hera placed her faithful guardian in the sky, where it still coils between the two Bears. Next to it is Hercules, kneeling with one foot on the dragon's head.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: ثعبان تنين: لادون حارس التفاح الذهبي.

stories.title: تنين الهسبريديس
stories.text: كان لادون الثعبان الذي لا ينام ملتفًّا حول شجرة التفاح الذهبي في حديقة الهسبريديس عند طرف العالم الغربي، وهي شجرة غرستها هيرا هدية عرس من الأرض. وكان على هرقل في عمله الحادي عشر أن يأتي بالتفاح، وفي روايات كثيرة قتل لادون ليحصل عليه. فرفعت هيرا حارسها الوفيّ إلى السماء، حيث ما زال يلتفّ بين الدبّين، وبجانبه هرقل جاثيًا وقدمه على رأس التنين.

egypt.seen: Taweret (also called Reret), a great hippopotamus goddess.

stories.title: The hippopotamus who guards the north
stories.text: Around the North Pole, Egyptian star maps show a huge female hippopotamus standing upright, with a crocodile on her back or a crocodile's tail. She is usually identified with stars of Draco and the Little Bear. Her role was to restrain the bull's foreleg of Set (the Big Dipper), holding it on a chain or a mooring post so it could not escape. She was also a protector of women in childbirth and of small children.
stories.source: Egyptian Streets, 'Ancient Egyptian constellations' (2024); Dendera zodiac

ar.seen: تاورت (وتسمّى أيضًا رِرِت)، إلهة فرس النهر العظيمة.

stories.title: فرس النهر التي تحرس الشمال
stories.text: تُظهر خرائط النجوم المصرية حول القطب الشمالي أنثى فرس نهر عظيمة واقفة، على ظهرها تمساح أو لها ذنب تمساح، وتُطابق عادة بنجوم من التنين والدب الأصغر. ودورها أن تُمسك ساق ثور ست (المغرفة) بسلسلة أو وتد رسوّ كي لا تفلت. وكانت أيضًا حامية النساء في الولادة وحامية الأطفال الصغار.

arab.seen: The Greek king Cepheus ("Qiqawus"). The name "al-Multahib", "the Inflamed One", is a translation, not an old Arab name. For the Arabs these stars were a pasture scene. A bright star is al-Ra'i, the shepherd, and a small star a cubit away is Kalb al-Ra'i, the shepherd's dog. Two bright stars are al-Firq, the flock. Faint stars all around are al-Sha' and al-Aghnam, the sheep. A hidden little star is al-Qurha, the white blaze on a horse's forehead, and a round cluster is al-Qidr, the cooking pot.

stories.title: The shepherd, his dog and his flock
stories.text: Arab star-lore filled this part of the northern sky with a whole pastoral camp. There is the shepherd (al-Ra'i) with his dog close by, and the sheep scattered around (al-Sha'). A pot is set out for cooking (al-Qidr), and a horse's white blaze (al-Qurha) shows nearby. Ibn Qutayba says simply: "The sheep are small stars between al-Qurha and al-Jady; the Shepherd is brighter than the sheep among them, and the Shepherd's Dog is a small star close to him." The star name Alrai (γ Cephei) still means "the shepherd".
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: After the stars already described come stars which the Greeks called
Qiqawus (Cepheus); but among the Arabs they are known as al-Multahib, the Inflamed One.
(Another reading: 'Qiqawus, and it may be called al-Multahib; and the Arabs call its stars the Sheep.')
The first of them is a small star with no light among the stars;
it is followed by a star of dazzling rays, the two a fathom apart;
and between this star and the first is a small star, not clearly seen,
a cubit away from it: the Arabs know it as the Shepherd's Dog;
you see it standing apart from its fellows; and the brightest they call the Shepherd.
The reporters disagree about the rest, and are not of one mind about them,
but I will mention what is sound and leave aside what is disputed and cast off.
On the shoulder of this figure you see a star, followed by small stars,
and a brilliant star above the belt, with stars in a row going before it;
two flashing, brilliant stars are called the stars of al-Firq, the Flock;
above them is a very small star, counted in the figure however you count it,
as if a veil were covering it: the Bedouins know it as al-Qurha, the white blaze.
Within this figure you see many small stars,
hidden and dim of body, known as the sheep and the flock.
Then on the hands of the Inflamed One you see two stars flashing like flame,
followed by small stars in a round, hollow patch
which those who know call the Cooking Pot. That is all I have heard told of it.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 20 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: هو الملك قيقاوس عند الروم، واسم «الملتهب» ترجمة وليس اسمًا عربيًا قديمًا. أما العرب فرأوا هنا مرعى: نجم نيّر هو الراعي، وكوكب صغير على ذراع منه هو كلب الراعي، ونجمان نيّران هما الفِرق أي القطيع، ونجوم خفية حولها هي الشاء والأغنام، وكويكب مستتر هو القُرحة، وكواكب مستديرة هي القِدر.

stories.title: الراعي وكلبه وغنمه
stories.text: ملأ العرب هذه الناحية من السماء الشمالية بمخيّم رعاة كامل: الراعي، وكلبه قريبًا منه، وغنمه منتشرة حوله، وقدرٌ منصوبة، وقُرحة فرس تلوح. يقول ابن قتيبة: «والشاء كواكب صغار فيما بين القرحة والجدي، والراعي أنور من كواكب الشاء بينها، وكلب الراعي كوكب صغير قريب منه». واسم النجم الحديث Alrai معناه «الراعي».

greek.seen: King Cepheus of Ethiopia, Andromeda's father.

stories.title: The king who sacrificed his daughter
stories.text: Cepheus ruled Ethiopia with his queen Cassiopeia. When she boasted that she was more beautiful than the sea-nymphs, Poseidon sent the monster Cetus to ravage the coast. An oracle said the only cure was to chain their daughter Andromeda to a rock as the monster's prey, and Cepheus agreed. Perseus arrived just in time to kill the monster. The whole family was later placed in the sky together: the king, the queen, the princess, the hero, and the monster.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: الملك قيفاوس ملك إثيوبيا، أبو أندروميدا.

stories.title: الملك الذي ضحّى بابنته
stories.text: حكم قيفاوس إثيوبيا مع ملكته كاسيوبيا. فلمّا تباهت بأنها أجمل من حوريات البحر أرسل بوسيدون الوحش قيطس يخرّب الساحل. وقالت العرّافة إن العلاج الوحيد أن تُقيَّد ابنتهما أندروميدا إلى صخرة طعامًا للوحش، فوافق قيفاوس. ووصل برسيوس في اللحظة الأخيرة فقتل الوحش. ثم رُفعت الأسرة كلها إلى السماء معًا: الملك والملكة والأميرة والبطل والوحش.

arab.seen: Boötes, which the Greeks called the herdsman shouting at his cattle; that's where the names "the Howler" and "the Cowherd" come from. It is also "the Guardian of the Sky" and "the Guardian of the North". The Arab names are these. The faint stars on its hand are al-Diba', the hyenas. The brilliant star is al-Simak al-Ramih, "the lofty one with the lance". Small stars beside it are al-Silah, its weapons, and two stars in front are Rayat al-Simak, its banner. Two stars on the heel are Rumh al-Simak (its lance) and 'Udhab (the lance's pennants).

stories.title: The armed Simak and the unarmed Simak
stories.text: The Arabs paired two bright stars, Arcturus and Spica, and called both al-Simak, "the high one". Arcturus has a little star in front of it, its "banner", so it became al-Ramih, the one carrying a lance. Spica has nothing in front of it, so it became al-A'zal, the unarmed man. As Ibn Qutayba explains, "al-A'zal is a man who has no weapon with him". In the Arab sky the two Simaks are the two shins of the giant Lion. The poet Ka'b ibn Zuhayr wrote: "When the two Farqads had turned, I urged her on, and the Simak with the weapon and the unarmed one blew."
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); al-Marzuqi, al-Azmina wa al-Amkina (11th c.)

full.e: Now we take up the stars of the Howler, which is called the Guardian of the Sky,
the Guardian of al-Simak, and of the North: these sayings were told to us
by trustworthy scholars of the stars, from a band of the sages of Greece;
and reports have reached us from them that it is also the Cymbal-player and the Cowherd.
Its first stars are small ones on the palm of this figure,
without light, without any gleam: the Bedouins know them as the Hyenas.
And there is a star like a flashing meteor; they named it al-Simak al-Ramih, the Lancer.
Of two stars in the middle of the figure, surrounded by small stars,
hidden, with dim forms: the Bedouins know these as the Weapons.
In front of it is one of two stars, close to two dim stars,
which the sharp-eyed can see: these are called the Banner of al-Simak.

a: و بعد هذا النجم ذي السناءِ
full.e: They lie on the belt of the Howler; and after this radiant star
comes a star, and behind it two stars, set upon the heel.
The two brighter ones, know it, are among the Arabs the Lance of al-Simak, and the two faint ones its pennants.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 14 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: العوّاء عند الروم رجل يرعى البقر ويصيح بها، ومنه أسماء العوّاء والصيّاح والبقّار، ويسمّى أيضًا حارس السماء وحارس الشمال. وأسماء العرب لنجومه: النجوم الخفية على راحته هي الضباع، والنجم الساطع السِّماك الرامح، وحوله كواكب صغيرة هي السلاح، ونجمان أمامه هما راية السِّماك، ونجمان على الكعب هما رمح السِّماك والعُذَب.

stories.title: السماك الرامح والسماك الأعزل
stories.text: جمع العرب بين نجمين نيّرين هما السماك الرامح والسماك الأعزل، ومعنى السماك المرتفع. فللرامح كوكب صغير بين يديه هو رايته فصار ذا رمح، والأعزل لا شيء بين يديه، قال ابن قتيبة: «والأعزل هو الرجل الذي لا سلاح معه». وفي سماء العرب السماكان ساقا الأسد العظيم. قال كعب بن زهير: «فلمّا استدار الفرقدان زجرتُها ... وهبّ سماكٌ ذو سلاحٍ وأعزلُ».

greek.seen: The herdsman or ploughman driving the Bear: Arcas, or Icarius.

stories.title: The bear-keeper and the first wine
stories.text: His bright star Arcturus means "bear-guard", because he seems to follow the Great Bear around the Pole. One story makes him Arcas, Callisto's son, still guarding his mother. Another makes him Icarius of Athens, whom the god Dionysus taught to make wine. Icarius shared it with some shepherds. They had never been drunk before, thought they had been poisoned, and killed him. His daughter Erigone found his body with the help of their dog Maera and died of grief. The gods placed all three in the sky: Icarius as Boötes, Erigone as Virgo, and the dog as Procyon or Sirius.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

poem.orig:
εὖτ᾽ ἂν δ᾽ Ὠρίων καὶ Σείριος ἐς μέσον ἔλθῃ
οὐρανόν, Ἀρκτοῦρον δ᾽ ἐσίδῃ ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠώς,
ὦ Πέρση, τότε πάντας ἀποδρέπεν οἴκαδε βότρυς.
poem.trans:
But when Orion and Sirius come into mid-heaven,
and rosy-fingered Dawn looks upon Arcturus,
then, Perses, cut off all the grape clusters and bring them home.
poem.by: Hesiod, Works and Days 609–611

ar.seen: الراعي أو الحرّاث يسوق الدب: أركاس أو إيكاريوس.

stories.title: حارس الدب وأول خمر
stories.text: نجمه اللامع أركتوروس معناه «حارس الدب»، لأنه يبدو كأنه يتبع الدب الأكبر حول القطب. وتجعله رواية أركاس ابن كاليستو يحرس أمه، وتجعله أخرى إيكاريوس الأثيني الذي علّمه الإله ديونيسوس صنع الخمر. فسقى إيكاريوس بعض الرعاة، ولم يكونوا قد سكروا من قبل فظنّوا أنهم سُمّموا فقتلوه. ووجدت ابنته إيريغوني جثّته بمساعدة كلبتهما مايرا فماتت حزنًا. فرفع الآلهة الثلاثة إلى السماء: إيكاريوس هو العوّاء، وإيريغوني هي العذراء، والكلبة هي الشعرى الشامية أو الشعرى اليمانية.

stories.title: The rain that becomes pearls
stories.text: Arcturus is Swati, the 15th lunar mansion. An old belief says that when rain falls while the Moon is in Swati, drops that fall into oyster shells become pearls, drops that fall into bamboo become a precious bamboo-sap, and drops caught by the chataka bird quench its thirst, because it drinks nothing else.
stories.source: Indian poetic tradition

ar.seen: سواتي، السيف (السماك الرامح).

stories.title: المطر الذي يصير لؤلؤًا
stories.text: السماك الرامح هو «سواتي»، المنزل الخامس عشر. وفي معتقد قديم أن المطر إذا نزل والقمر في سواتي فإن القطرات التي تقع في المحار تصير لؤلؤًا، والتي تقع في الخيزران تصير عصارة خيزران نفيسة، والتي يتلقّاها طائر التشاتاكا تروي عطشه لأنه لا يشرب غيرها.

safrica.seen: Swazi: Arcturus is Lweti.

stories.title: The star that calls the women to work
stories.text: The Swazi call Arcturus Lweti. When it appears before sunrise in November, women start their work in the fields.
stories.source: Astronomical Society of Southern Africa, 'African Ethnoastronomy' (after P. G. Alcock, Venus Rising, 2014)

af.seen: Swazi: Arcturus is Lweti.

stories.title: Die ster wat die vroue werk toe roep
stories.text: Die Swazi noem Arcturus Lweti. Wanneer hy in November voor sonop verskyn, begin die vroue met hul werk op die lande.

ar.seen: السوازي: السماك الرامح «لويتي».

stories.title: النجم الذي يدعو النساء إلى العمل
stories.text: يسمّي السوازي السماك الرامح «لويتي»، فإذا ظهر قبل الشروق في نوفمبر بدأت النساء عملهن في الحقول.

arab.seen: The Northern Crown: a ring of dim stars with one brighter star in the middle. The Arabs called it al-Fakka. The poet says ordinary people in every city call it Qas'at al-Aytam, "the orphans' bowl". Scholars call it the Crown (al-Iklil), and the Greeks gave it that name too. He frankly says he knows no older Bedouin name for it.

stories.title: The broken bowl of the poor
stories.text: The stars of al-Fakka form a near-circle with a gap on one side. People pictured it as a wooden bowl with a chip broken out of its rim, the kind of bowl that only the poor or orphans would keep using, because they couldn't afford a new one. So it was called Qas'at al-Masakin ("the bowl of the poor") or Qas'at al-Yatama ("the orphans' bowl"). Even the name al-Fakka carries the idea of something broken open.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib)

full.e: After the Howler we mention al-Fakka, stars that have lost their light,
known to young and old, with one bright star among them,
and the common folk in every town call them the Orphans' Bowl.
With the scholars of the stars they were named the Crown, and among the Greeks;
of the Bedouins I have no report about them, or I would have mentioned it.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 5 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: الإكليل الشمالي: حلقة من نجوم خافتة بينها كوكب منير. تسمّيها العرب الفَكّة، ويقول الناظم إن العوام في كل مصر يسمّونها قصعة الأيتام، وأهل العلم يسمّونها الإكليل كما سمّاها الروم. ويعترف بأنه لا يعرف لها اسمًا قديمًا عند الأعراب.

stories.title: قصعة المساكين
stories.text: نجوم الفكّة تكاد تكون دائرة وفي أحد جانبيها فُرجة. فتخيّلها الناس قصعة من خشب انكسر طرفها، وهي القصعة التي لا يبقى يستعملها إلا الفقراء أو الأيتام لأنهم لا يملكون بدلها قصعة صحيحة، فسمّوها «قصعة المساكين» و«قصعة اليتامى». وفي اسم الفكّة نفسه معنى الانفكاك والانكسار.

greek.seen: The golden crown of Ariadne.

stories.title: Ariadne's crown
stories.text: Ariadne, princess of Crete, fell in love with Theseus and gave him the thread that led him out of the Minotaur's labyrinth. He sailed away with her but abandoned her asleep on the island of Naxos. The god Dionysus found her there weeping, and she agreed to marry him. As a wedding gift he gave her a golden crown made by Hephaestus. When she died he threw it up into the heavens, where its jewels became the ring of stars.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Ovid, Metamorphoses 8

ar.seen: التاج الذهبي لأريادني.

stories.title: تاج أريادني
stories.text: أحبّت أريادني أميرة كريت ثيسيوس وأعطته الخيط الذي أخرجه من متاهة المينوتور. فأبحر بها ثم تركها نائمة على جزيرة ناكسوس. فوجدها الإله ديونيسوس تبكي، فقبلت الزواج منه، وأهداها تاجًا ذهبيًا صنعه هيفايستوس. ولمّا ماتت رمى التاج إلى السماء فصارت جواهره حلقة النجوم.

arab.seen: Hercules, "the one kneeling on his knee". A star on his brow is Kalb al-Ra'i, the shepherd's dog, next to the bright al-Ra'i (the shepherd), which sits on the Snake-Charmer's forehead. A line of stars across his hands and chest is al-Nasaq al-Shami, "the northern row". Dim, scattered stars between his leg and his belt are al-Diba', the hyenas, and bright stars around his left foot are al-Tamathil, "the statues".

stories.title: Hyenas around the camp
stories.text: Ibn Qutayba lists a whole family of hyenas in this region. Al-Diba', the hyenas, are scattered stars below the Daughters of Na'sh, with Awlad al-Diba', the cubs, beside them. Al-Dhikh, the big red male hyena, sits between the Daughters of Na'sh and the Falling Eagle. Together with the wolves in Draco and the shepherd and his dog nearby, the northern sky becomes a desert night full of herds and the animals that hunt them. (The shepherd's story continues under Ophiuchus.)
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: We mention the one Kneeling on his Knee, and all we know of his figure.
The first of his stars that we mention is a star on his forehead or his brow;
the Bedouins named it the Shepherd's Dog, near a shining, flashing star
known as the Shepherd, whose light sits above the forehead of the Snake-Charmer;
its mention will come later, when the count reaches the Snake-Charmer.
It is followed by stars in a row, with little light and faintness in them;
they were named the Northern Row, and they follow the Orphans' Bowl.
These stars that we have mentioned lie on the hands and chest of this figure,
as though lined up in a row, appearing to the watcher when the night grows dark.
And one of the people of this science said that the stars you see
between the shape of its leg and the belt (dim stars, scattered),
are known among the Arabs as the Hyenas; they are followed by a star in the place of the heel
of its left foot, and it is called al-Nasaq, the Row; all agree on it in the books of the anwa',
and that around it are blazing stars known among the Arabs as the Statues.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 14 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: الجاثي على ركبتيه (هرقل). نجم على جبهته هو كلب الراعي قرب الراعي النيّر الذي فوق جبين الحوّاء. وكواكب مصطفّة على يديه وصدره هي النسق الشامي، ونجوم طمس متفرقة بين رجله وحزامه هي الضباع، وكواكب حول قدمه اليسرى هي التماثيل.

stories.title: ضباع حول المخيّم
stories.text: يذكر ابن قتيبة أسرة كاملة من الضباع في هذه الناحية: «الضباع» كواكب مختلفة أسفل من بنات نعش، و«أولاد الضباع» كواكب صغار عن يمينها، و«الذِّيخ» كوكب أحمر فوق الضباع بين بنات نعش والنسر الواقع. فإذا أضفت إليها الذئبين في التنين والراعي وكلبه، صارت السماء الشمالية ليلة من ليالي البادية فيها القطعان ومن يتربّص بها. (وتتمة حكاية الراعي في كوكبة الحوّاء.)

greek.seen: Heracles, kneeling, with his foot on the dragon's head.

stories.title: The kneeling hero
stories.text: The earliest Greeks did not know who this figure was and simply called him Engonasin, "the one on his knees". Later writers decided he was Heracles, kneeling with his club raised and one foot on the head of Ladon, the dragon of the Hesperides (Draco), during his eleventh labour. Hera drove Heracles mad, and he was given twelve labours to earn forgiveness.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia; Kitab al-Sama'

ar.seen: هرقل جاثيًا وقدمه على رأس التنين.

stories.title: البطل الجاثي
stories.text: لم يعرف أقدم الإغريق من هذه الصورة، فسمّوها «الجاثي على ركبتيه». ثم قرّر الكتّاب المتأخرون أنه هرقل جاثيًا رافعًا هراوته وقدمه على رأس لادون تنين الهسبريديس في عمله الحادي عشر. وقد أصابت هيرا هرقل بالجنون، وكُلّف اثني عشر عملًا لينال الصفح.

arab.seen: Lyra. The poet lists all its foreign names: al-Sulyaq (from the Greek word for lyre), the Goose, the Harp, the Cymbal, the Tortoise and al-Lura' (Lyra). The commentary notes these all come from Greek tradition. The Arab part is the three bright stars called al-Nasr, the Eagle. The brightest of them is Vega, al-Nasr al-Waqi', "the eagle swooping down".

stories.title: The eagle that folds its wings
stories.text: The Arabs saw two eagles facing each other across the Milky Way. Vega, with two smaller stars beside it, is al-Nasr al-Waqi', the eagle dropping onto its prey. Ibn Qutayba says: "They say the two stars are its wings, which it has folded in as it swoops." Across the river of the Milky Way is the other eagle, which has spread its wings and is flying (see Aquila). The name Vega comes from (al-Nasr) al-Waqi'.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: Now we mention, in order, stars known as al-Sulyaq, the lyre,
and as the Goose, know it, and the Harp; those who know call it the Cymbal,
and the Tortoise, and al-Lura' (Lyra): so the books of the anwa' tell.
Stars that you see shining, three of which are called the Eagle;
among them a bright and famous star, with dazzling light and radiance,
that snatches the eye with its gleam: the Arabs know it as the Falling Eagle.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 6 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: السلياق، وقد ذكر الناظم أسماءها الأجنبية كلها: السلياق (من اليونانية بمعنى القيثارة) والأوز والمعزفة والصنج والسلحفاة واللوراء، وهي كلها مأخوذة من تراث الإغريق. أما الاسم العربي فهو الكواكب الثلاثة النيّرة المسمّاة النسر، وأنورها النسر الواقع.

stories.title: النسر الذي ضمّ جناحيه
stories.text: رأى العرب نسرين يتقابلان على جانبي المجرة. فالنسر الواقع كوكب منير خلفه كوكبان أصغر منه، قال ابن قتيبة: «ويقولون هما جناحاه، وقد ضمّهما إليه حين وقع». وعلى الضفة الأخرى من نهر المجرة النسر الآخر قد بسط جناحيه وطار (انظر العقاب). واسم Vega الحديث مأخوذ من «الواقع».

greek.seen: The lyre of Orpheus.

stories.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
stories.text: Hermes made the first lyre from a tortoise shell, and Apollo gave it to Orpheus, whose music could charm animals, trees and even stones. When his wife Eurydice died of a snakebite, Orpheus went down to the underworld and sang until Hades let her go. There was one condition: he must not look back at her until they reached the world above. Just before the end, he turned to look, and she slipped back into the dark for ever. After Orpheus died, the Muses placed his lyre among the stars.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Ovid, Metamorphoses 10

ar.seen: قيثارة أورفيوس.

stories.title: أورفيوس ويوريديكي
stories.text: صنع هرمس أول قيثارة من صدفة سلحفاة، وأهداها أبولو إلى أورفيوس الذي كانت موسيقاه تسحر الحيوان والشجر بل الحجر. ولمّا ماتت زوجته يوريديكي بلدغة أفعى نزل أورفيوس إلى العالم السفلي وغنّى حتى أذن هاديس بعودتها، بشرط واحد: ألّا ينظر إليها حتى يبلغا العالم العلوي. وقبيل النهاية التفت لينظر، فانزلقت عائدة إلى الظلام إلى الأبد. وبعد موت أورفيوس وضعت ربّات الفنون قيثارته بين النجوم.

stories.title: The Weaver Girl and the Cowherd
stories.text: Zhinü, a heavenly weaver and granddaughter of the Queen Mother of the West, fell in love with Niulang, a poor cowherd, and married him. Furious, the Queen Mother drew her hairpin across the sky and made a great river, the Milky Way, to separate them for ever: Vega on one side, Altair on the other. Once a year, on the seventh night of the seventh month, magpies fly up and make a bridge so the lovers can meet. This is the Qixi festival, still celebrated today. The Japanese Tanabata comes from this story.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; traditional

poem.orig:
迢迢牵牛星，皎皎河汉女。
纤纤擢素手，札札弄机杼。
终日不成章，泣涕零如雨。
河汉清且浅，相去复几许？
盈盈一水间，脉脉不得语。
poem.trans:
Far, far away, the Herd-Boy star; bright, bright, the Girl of the Silver River.
Slender, slender, she lifts her white hands; click, clack, she works the shuttle of her loom.
All day she cannot finish a pattern; her tears fall like rain.
The Silver River is clear and shallow; how far apart can they be?
Only a single brimming stream between them, gazing, gazing, and unable to speak.
poem.by: Nineteen Old Poems, no. 10 (Han dynasty)

ar.seen: جينيو، فتاة النسيج (النسر الواقع).

stories.title: فتاة النسيج وراعي البقر
stories.text: أحبّت جينيو النسّاجة السماوية، حفيدة ملكة الغرب الأم، راعيَ بقر فقيرًا اسمه نيولانغ وتزوّجته. فغضبت ملكة الغرب الأم وجرّت دبّوس شعرها عبر السماء فصنعت نهرًا عظيمًا هو درب التبانة يفصل بينهما إلى الأبد: النسر الواقع على ضفّة والنسر الطائر على الأخرى. ومرة في السنة، في الليلة السابعة من الشهر السابع، تطير طيور العقعق فتصنع جسرًا يلتقي عليه الحبيبان. وهذا عيد «تشي شي» الذي ما زال يُحتفل به، ومنه جاء عيد تاناباتا الياباني.

stories.title: Tanabata
stories.text: The princess Tanabata (Orihime), daughter of the king of the gods, fell in love with a mortal, Kengyū (Hikoboshi). Her father raised them into the sky as two stars and separated them with the river of the Milky Way. They may meet only once a year, on the seventh day of the seventh month, when birds gather to make a bridge between them. On Tanabata, people in Japan write wishes on strips of coloured paper and hang them on bamboo branches. The story came to Japan from the Chinese tale of the Weaver Girl and the Cowherd.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama' p. 127

ar.seen: أوريهيمه، الأميرة النسّاجة (النسر الواقع).

stories.title: تاناباتا
stories.text: أحبّت الأميرة تاناباتا (أوريهيمه) ابنة ملك الآلهة رجلًا من البشر هو كينغيو (هيكوبوشي)، فرفعهما أبوها إلى السماء نجمين وفصل بينهما بنهر درب التبانة. ولا يلتقيان إلا مرة في السنة، في اليوم السابع من الشهر السابع، حين تجتمع الطيور فتصنع جسرًا بينهما. وفي عيد تاناباتا يكتب اليابانيون أمنياتهم على شرائط ورق ملوّن ويعلّقونها على أغصان الخيزران. وقد جاءت القصة إلى اليابان من حكاية فتاة النسيج وراعي البقر الصينية.

india.seen: Abhijit, the 'victorious' star (Vega), the lost 28th nakshatra.

stories.title: The star that slipped from its place
stories.text: In the oldest lists there were 28 lunar mansions, and Vega was the 28th, Abhijit, 'the victorious'. The Mahabharata tells that Abhijit slipped from its place in the sky, and the gods replaced it with the Krittikas (the Pleiades). Later lists counted only 27, and Abhijit was left out.
stories.source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva

ar.seen: أبهيجيت، النجم «المنتصر» (النسر الواقع)، المنزل الثامن والعشرون المفقود.

stories.title: النجم الذي انزلق من مكانه
stories.text: كانت منازل القمر في أقدم القوائم ثمانية وعشرين، والنسر الواقع هو الثامن والعشرون «أبهيجيت» أي المنتصر. وتحكي المهابهاراتا أن أبهيجيت انزلق من مكانه في السماء فوضع الآلهة الكريتيكا (الثريا) مكانه، ثم صارت القوائم المتأخرة سبعة وعشرين وتُرك أبهيجيت.

safrica.seen: /Gwi San: Vega is the male steenbok.

stories.title: The steenbok pair
stories.text: The /Gwi San call Vega the male steenbok and Altair (in Aquila) the female steenbok, two small antelope on either side of the Milky Way.
stories.source: Astronomical Society of Southern Africa, 'African Ethnoastronomy' (after P. G. Alcock, Venus Rising, 2014)

af.seen: /Gwi San: Vega is die steenbokram.

stories.title: Die steenbokpaar
stories.text: Die /Gwi San noem Vega die steenbokram en Altair (in Aquila) die steenbokooi, twee klein bokkies aan weerskante van die Melkweg.

ar.seen: سان /غوي: النسر الواقع ذكر الستينبوك.

stories.title: زوج الستينبوك
stories.text: يسمّي سان /غوي النسر الواقع ذكر الستينبوك، والنسر الطائر (في العقاب) أنثاه، ظبيين صغيرين على جانبي درب التبانة.

arab.seen: Cygnus, which the Greeks called the bird and which Arabic astronomy called "the Hen". The Bedouin saw riders here. Four stars in a row are al-Fawaris, the horsemen, and the fifth, a great bright star, is al-Ridf, the rider sitting behind (Deneb). They rise with the Milky Way, near Lyra and its Falling Eagle.

stories.title: The horsemen crossing the river
stories.text: Ibn Qutayba describes five stars "in a line, cutting across the Milky Way". They are the Fawaris, horsemen fording the great river of the sky. Behind them, in the Milky Way, is al-Ridf, a rider sitting pillion on the back of a horse. Desert travellers steered by them. An old verse advises a rider at night: "Keep the Ridf of the Horsemen on your right, and the returning Ostriches on your left."
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib)

full.e: After the figure of Lyra we mention stars set evenly in a row,
known as the Bird and the Hen, as though they were blazing meteors.
Four of them are known as the Horsemen, and al-Ridf, know it, is the name of the fifth;
al-Ridf is a great, shining star, with the four stars riding in front of it.
If you want to see them once, they rise together with the Milky Way,
close to the stars of Lyra and its bright Falling Eagle.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 6 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: الطائر أو الدجاجة. ورأى أهل البادية هنا فرسانًا: أربعة كواكب مصطفّة هي الفوارس، والخامس كوكب نيّر عظيم هو الرِّدف، أي الراكب خلف صاحبه. وتطلع مع المجرة قرب السلياق ونسرها الواقع.

stories.title: الفوارس يعبرون النهر
stories.text: يصف ابن قتيبة خمسة كواكب «مصطفّة قد قطعت المجرة عرضًا» هي الفوارس كأنهم يخوضون نهر السماء، وخلفهم في المجرة «الردف» الراكب وراء الفارس. وكان المسافرون يهتدون بها، وفي بيت قديم: «ضعي رِدفَ الفوارس عن يمينٍ ... وصادرةَ النعائم عن شمالِ».

greek.seen: A swan: Zeus in disguise, or Orpheus.

stories.title: The swan
stories.text: Zeus took the form of a swan to visit Leda, queen of Sparta, and from that meeting came the twins Castor and Pollux and the beautiful Helen. The swan was set in the sky in memory of the disguise. Another story says the swan is Orpheus himself, turned into a bird after his death and placed next to his lyre. A third story says it is Cycnus, who dived again and again into a river to recover the body of his friend Phaethon.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia; Ovid, Metamorphoses 2

ar.seen: بجعة: زيوس متنكّرًا، أو أورفيوس.

stories.title: البجعة
stories.text: تنكّر زيوس في صورة بجعة ليزور ليدا ملكة إسبرطة، فكان من ذلك التوأمان كاستور وبولوكس وهيلين الجميلة، ووُضعت البجعة في السماء ذكرى لهذا التنكّر. وتقول رواية أخرى إن البجعة أورفيوس نفسه، حُوّل طائرًا بعد موته ووُضع قرب قيثارته. وتقول ثالثة إنها كيكنوس الذي ظلّ يغوص في النهر مرة بعد مرة ليستخرج جثة صديقه فايثون.

arab.seen: Cassiopeia, "the Lady of the Chair". For the Arabs, though, these stars were a great she-camel. A bright star on its hump is al-Kaff al-Khadib, "the henna-dyed hand", and other stars lie on the camel's saddle, thighs and tail. Faint stars form the camel's neck, its head joins the stars of Andromeda, and two stars are on its foot. A cloudy patch is like a brand on its thigh. The poet adds that the ancients and the astrologers saw instead a young woman raised on a throne.

stories.title: Al-Thurayya's henna-dyed hand
stories.text: The Arabs imagined al-Thurayya (the Pleiades) as a beautiful girl stretching out two long arms. Her right hand reaches far to the north and ends here: the bright W of Cassiopeia is her palm, painted with henna, al-Kaff al-Khadib. Her other, shorter hand is the "cut-off hand" that reaches down to Cetus. A poet describes the Eagle (Vega) "flying up from the henna-dyed hand" as the night turns. The star name Caph (β Cassiopeiae) is all that is left of Kaff, "hand".
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.); Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib); Kitab al-Sama'

full.e: After this we mention the Lady of the Chair, stars likened to a strong she-camel;
you see them gleaming and glittering, one of them upon the camel's hump,

a: وهو عظيم الجرم ذو نور يَقق
full.e: great in body, with pure white light; it follows the Eagle when the Eagle rises,
and among the Arabs it is called the Henna-Dyed Hand; it appears in their poems and their speeches.
Beneath it are bright stars, all of them within the figure:
some lie on the camel's saddle, and some on its thighs and tail.

a: قد شُبِّهت وعند من قد نجما
full.e: These stars, among the ancients and those who study the stars, have been likened
to a graceful maiden raised up on a throne, as the trusted expert has related.
From the Henna-Dyed Hand begin stars in a row, all of them dim;
they do not glitter when they shine; they make them the neck of the she-camel,
and its head is stars joined to the neck, from the stars of the Chained Woman;
and two of its stars lie on the camel's foot-pad,

a: قد جعلت في فخذ العنس سمة
full.e: and a dim patch called 'the cloudy one' has been set as a brand on the camel's thigh.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 13 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: ذات الكرسي. لكن العرب رأت في نجومها ناقة عظيمة: نجم نيّر على سنامها هو الكف الخضيب، ونجوم على قتبها وفخذيها وذنبها، ونجوم خافتة هي عنقها، ورأسها متصل بنجوم المرأة المسلسلة، ونجمان على منسمها، ولطخة سحابية كالوسم على فخذها. ويذكر الناظم أن القدماء والمنجّمين شبّهوها بغادة مرفوعة على سرير.

stories.title: كفّ الثريا المخضوبة
stories.text: تخيّل العرب الثريا فتاة جميلة لها كفّان ممدودتان: الطويلة إلى الشمال تنتهي هنا، فالحرف W الذي تصنعه ذات الكرسي هو كفّها المخضوبة بالحنّاء، «الكف الخضيب». والأخرى قصيرة هي «الكف الجذماء» تمتد إلى قيطس. ويصف أحد الشعراء النسر «طار عن كفّ الخضيب» مع دوران الليل. واسم النجم الحديث Caph بقية من كلمة «كف».

greek.seen: Queen Cassiopeia on her throne.

stories.title: The boastful queen
stories.text: Queen Cassiopeia of Ethiopia boasted that she (or her daughter Andromeda) was more beautiful than the Nereids, the nymphs of the sea. To punish her, Poseidon sent a flood and the monster Cetus. She was placed in the sky sitting on her throne, but as a final humiliation the throne circles the Pole, so for half the year she hangs upside down.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: الملكة كاسيوبيا على عرشها.

stories.title: الملكة المتباهية
stories.text: تباهت كاسيوبيا ملكة إثيوبيا بأنها (أو ابنتها أندروميدا) أجمل من النيريدات حوريات البحر، فأرسل بوسيدون عقابًا لها طوفانًا والوحش قيطس. ووُضعت في السماء جالسة على عرشها، لكن عرشها يدور حول القطب إذلالًا أخيرًا لها، فتظلّ نصف السنة معلّقة رأسًا على عقب.

stories.title: The anchor
stories.text: Fishermen in Japan saw the W of Cassiopeia as an anchor, Ikari-boshi, or as a mountain shape. Because it stays in the northern sky across from the Big Dipper, it helped them find north.
stories.source: Japanese star folklore collected by Nojiri Hōei

ar.seen: إيكاري-بوشي، نجم المرساة.

stories.title: المرساة
stories.text: رأى الصيّادون في اليابان حرف W في ذات الكرسي مرساة «إيكاري-بوشي» أو شكل جبل، ولأنه يبقى في السماء الشمالية مقابل المغرفة كان يساعدهم على معرفة الشمال.

arab.seen: Perseus, a tall man holding the head of a monster, which in Arabic became Ra's al-Ghul, "the ghoul's head" (Algol). The Arabs saw these stars as part of al-Thurayya's arm. A faint cloudy star (the Double Cluster) is Mi'sam al-Thurayya, her wrist, and the bright star on Perseus' side is Mirfaq al-Thurayya, her elbow (Mirfak). Two stars are al-'Adud, the upper arm, and there are al-Ma'bid (the inside of the knee) and al-Ibra (the needle). Two stars by his foot are 'Atiq al-Najm, "the shoulder of the Pleiades".

stories.title: The arm of al-Thurayya
stories.text: In the Arab sky, al-Thurayya is a girl, and her right arm stretches up through Perseus. Her wrist is a misty patch of stars, her elbow is the bright star Mirfak (still called that from Mirfaq, "elbow"), and her shoulder is 'Atiq al-Najm, near her body in Taurus. Her henna-painted hand is in Cassiopeia. Al-Najm, "the Star", was the Arabs' usual name for al-Thurayya. Ibn Kathir notes that early commentators explained the Quranic oath "By the Star when it falls" (53:1) as al-Thurayya setting at dawn.
stories.source: Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib); Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: After it comes the Bearer of the Ghoul's Head, the figure of a man very tall,
like a long-limbed human, holding in his hand a ghoul with a huge head;
among the stars these stars are called Barshawush (Perseus) by the Greeks.
The first of them is a star of hidden light, hidden from the one who looks for it in the sky;
the Greeks know it as 'the cloudy one'; and the Bedouins call it,
as we have heard, the Wrist of al-Thurayya; I learned nothing else about it.
It lies on the forearm of this figure, followed by bright stars,
among them a shining, flashing star, with rays when you look at it;
it lies in Perseus' side, but the Arabs make it,
as we have heard, the Elbow of al-Thurayya; it is followed by a star that shines
close to it in its grandeur, called by the Greeks the Ghoul's Head.
After this star come two stars of Perseus' figure, both dim;
it has come from the Bedouins and the observers that they are called the Upper Arm.
Below the side you see two stars, leaning from it toward the Ghoul;
the higher is al-Ma'bid, the hollow of the knee, nearer to the elbow of the bright, awe-inspiring star,
and the other star is called the Needle; both lie in the middle of the Milky Way.
After this star come two stars, close to the Ghoul;
both are a foot of this figure, and around them are many stars,
some shining, some dim, with bright stars standing out among them;
two of them are known by the name 'Atiq al-Najm, the Shoulder of the Pleiades.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 20 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: برشاوش، رجل طويل يحمل رأس غول، ومنه اسم رأس الغول. ورأت العرب في نجومه ذراع الثريا: نجم سحابي هو معصم الثريا، والنجم النيّر في جنبه هو مرفق الثريا، ونجمان هما العضد، وفيه المأبض والإبرة، ونجمان عند قدمه هما عاتق النجم، أي عاتق الثريا.

stories.title: ذراع الثريا
stories.text: الثريا في سماء العرب فتاة تمتد ذراعها اليمنى إلى أعلى عبر برشاوش: معصمها لطخة من النجوم، ومرفقها النجم النيّر الذي ما زال يسمّى Mirfak من «المرفق»، وعاتقها «عاتق النجم» قرب جسدها في الثور، وكفّها المخضوبة في ذات الكرسي. و«النجم» هو اسم الثريا عند العرب، وقد ذكر ابن كثير أن من المفسرين من قال في قوله تعالى ﴿والنجم إذا هوى﴾: هي الثريا إذا سقطت مع الفجر.

greek.seen: The hero Perseus, holding the head of Medusa.

stories.title: Perseus and Medusa
stories.text: Perseus was sent to bring back the head of Medusa, a Gorgon with snakes for hair whose gaze turned people to stone. With a polished shield from Athena, winged sandals and a curved sword, he cut off her head while watching only her reflection. On his way home he saw Andromeda chained to a rock, about to be eaten by a sea monster. He turned the monster to stone with Medusa's head and married Andromeda. The star Algol marks the Gorgon's head.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Ovid, Metamorphoses 4

ar.seen: البطل برسيوس يحمل رأس ميدوسا.

stories.title: برسيوس وميدوسا
stories.text: أُرسل برسيوس ليأتي برأس ميدوسا، الغورغونة التي شعرها أفاعٍ ونظرتها تحوّل الناس حجارة. فبترس مصقول من أثينا وصندل مجنّح وسيف مقوّس قطع رأسها وهو ينظر إلى صورتها في الترس فقط. وفي طريق عودته رأى أندروميدا مقيّدة إلى صخرة على وشك أن يلتهمها وحش البحر، فحوّل الوحش حجرًا برأس ميدوسا وتزوّج أندروميدا. ونجم رأس الغول (Algol) يدلّ على رأس الغورغونة.

arab.seen: Auriga, the Greek charioteer holding the reins, who also carries a goat and two kids (from this came the Arabic name al-'Annaz, "the goat-keeper"). An empty patch of sky next to the Gazelles is al-Khiba', the tent. Its great star, Capella, is al-'Ayyuq, which rises before Aldebaran ("al-Fanīq") and is also called Raqib al-Najm, "the watcher of the Pleiades". It appears in the poetry of Khuwaylid ibn Khalid (Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali) and in proverbs. Three stars in a long triangle are the She-Goat and the Two Kids.

stories.title: Al-'Ayyuq, the one who stands in the way
stories.text: Al-'Ayyuq is part of the story of al-Thurayya and al-Dabaran (see Taurus). The name comes from the Arabic root '-w-q, "to hinder". Capella rises in the north-east ahead of Aldebaran and stands between him and the Pleiades, as if it were blocking the poor suitor from ever reaching the girl he loves. Because it seems to keep watch over her, it was also called her "watcher". It became proverbial for anything out of reach: the Arabs said "farther than the hanging place of al-'Ayyuq".
stories.source: Arabic lexicographers; al-Maydani, Majma' al-Amthal (12th c.); the Urjuza

full.e: It is followed by the stars of the Goat-keeper, which in the Hijaz are known
as the Holder of the Banner and of the Reins, their light piercing the veils of the dark.
On his head you see two stars, two dim hand-spans apart,
surrounded by many stars which the observers have not recorded,
in a patch of the sky empty of bright, visible stars,
all joined to the Gazelles: the Bedouins have long known them as the Tent.
Among them is a shining, mighty star, beside whose size the other stars look small;
it rises before the rising of al-Fanīq: the Bedouins know it as al-'Ayyuq,
and it is sometimes called the Watcher of the Pleiades; so the learned report.
It is the star that Khuwaylid ibn Khalid mentioned before us in his poetry,

a: و هو على منكب ذى الشمال
full.e: and others mention it in proverbs; it sits on the shoulder of the Holder of the Reins.
It is followed by a star smaller in size, yet not hidden or dim,
and after it two stars follow, resembling it in fullness of light;
they lie in a long triangle, rising after the rising of the Ghoul.
The desert people know the single one of them as the She-Goat, and I have heard
both of the two that follow the She-Goat called the Two Kids.
And all these gleaming stars are known as the Banners and the Followers.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 17 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: ممسك الأعنة، سائق العربة عند الإغريق يحمل عنزًا وجديين، ومنه اسم «العنّاز». وبقعة خالية بجوار الظباء هي الخِباء. ونجمها العظيم العيّوق يطلع قبل الدبران (الفنيق) ويسمّى رقيب النجم، وقد ذكره خويلد بن خالد (أبو ذؤيب الهذلي) في شعره وورد في الأمثال. وثلاثة كواكب على مثلث طويل هي العنز والجديان.

stories.title: العيّوق الذي يعوق
stories.text: العيّوق جزء من حكاية الثريا والدبران (انظر الثور). واسمه من «عاق يعوق» أي منع، لأنه يطلع في الشمال الشرقي قبل الدبران ويقف بينه وبين الثريا، كأنه يمنع العاشق الفقير من الوصول إلى من يحب. ولأنه كأنه يحرسها سُمّي رقيبها. وصار مثلًا لما لا يُنال، فقالت العرب: «أبعد من مناط العيّوق».

greek.seen: The charioteer, carrying a she-goat and her kids.

stories.title: The charioteer and the goat
stories.text: The Charioteer is usually Erichthonius, a king of Athens who was said to have invented the four-horse chariot, and who was placed in the sky for it. He carries a she-goat on his shoulder: Amalthea, the goat whose milk nursed the infant Zeus on Crete. Her star is Capella, "the little she-goat", and two small stars beside it are her kids.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: سائق العربة يحمل عنزًا وجديين.

stories.title: السائق والعنز
stories.text: سائق العربة في الغالب هو إريختونيوس ملك أثينا الذي قيل إنه اخترع العربة ذات الخيول الأربعة فرُفع إلى السماء لذلك. ويحمل على كتفه عنزًا هي أمالثيا التي أرضعت زيوس الطفل بلبنها في كريت، ونجمها العيّوق (Capella أي «العنيزة الصغيرة»)، والنجمان الصغيران بجانبها جدياها.

safrica.seen: Zulu: Capella is iNtshola, 'the cattle thief'. !Kung: 'green leaf horn'.

stories.title: The cattle thief
stories.text: The Zulu call Capella iNtshola, 'the cattle thief'. For the !Kung San it is the 'green leaf horn': when it appears, the first flowers of the rainy season are on their way.
stories.source: Astronomical Society of Southern Africa, 'African Ethnoastronomy' (after P. G. Alcock, Venus Rising, 2014)

af.seen: Zoeloe: Capella is iNtshola, 'die beesdief'. !Kung: 'groenblaar-horing'.

stories.title: Die beesdief
stories.text: Die Zoeloe noem Capella iNtshola, 'die beesdief'. Vir die !Kung San is hy die 'groenblaar-horing': wanneer hy verskyn, is die eerste blomme van die reënseisoen op pad.

ar.seen: الزولو: العيّوق «إنتشولا» سارق الماشية. الكونغ: «قرن الورقة الخضراء».

stories.title: سارق الماشية
stories.text: يسمّي الزولو العيّوق «إنتشولا» أي سارق الماشية. وهو عند سان الكونغ «قرن الورقة الخضراء»: إذا ظهر فأولى أزهار موسم المطر في الطريق.

arab.seen: Ophiuchus, the Snake-Charmer, gripping a speckled serpent. A star on his nose is al-Ra'i, the shepherd (Rasalhague), which forms a triangle with the two Eagles, and a bright star on his shoulder is Kalb al-Ra'i, the shepherd's dog. A long line of bright stars runs from the Kneeling Man's wrist along the snake to the Charmer's fingers; this is al-Nasaq al-Yamani, "the southern row". The dim stars between it and the northern row are al-Aghnam, the sheep, and the whole area is al-Rawda, "the meadow". The smallest stars are al-Naqad, a breed of small sheep.

stories.title: The shepherd in the meadow
stories.text: Between Hercules and Ophiuchus the Arabs saw a fenced pasture. Two long rows of stars, al-Nasaqan, "the two rows", run like fences into the Milky Way: one northern, one southern. Ibn Qutayba writes: "In the middle of the two rows is a star called the Shepherd, and what lies between the two rows is called the Meadow." The shepherd stands with his dog at his side, his sheep graze among the faint stars inside the fences, and hyenas and wolves prowl in the dark beyond (see Hercules and Draco). It is one of the most complete scenes in the Arab sky.
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: It is followed by the stars of the Snake-Charmer, with a speckled serpent in his hand;
his whole figure has already been told of, in the figure of the one Kneeling on his Knee.
The first of his stars that we mention is a star on his nose or his mouth;
together with the two Eagles it lies flat, in the form of a drawn triangle;
the Bedouins know it as the Shepherd; and after it, from the Holder of the Serpent,
comes a radiant star on his shoulder, which the Arabs call the Shepherd's Dog.
Beginning from the wrist of the Kneeling Man, upon his knee, are stars full of brilliance,
joining in a line of shining stars, bright, their bodies dazzling,
some on the serpent and some on the fingers of the Charmer, and all of them with light;
they fill the watcher's eye in the dark: they named them the Southern Row.
And some people said that the name covers all the stars you see
between it and the Northern Row, apart from those I described as the Sheep;
and the whole patch is known as the Meadow; and I have heard its dim little stars called the small sheep.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 13 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: الحوّاء يمسك حيّة رقشاء. نجم على أنفه هو الراعي ويصنع مع النسرين مثلثًا، ونجم نيّر على منكبه هو كلب الراعي. وخطّ طويل من نجوم زاهرة يبتدئ من معصم الجاثي ويمر على الحية وأنامل الحوّاء هو النسق اليماني. والنجوم الخافتة بينه وبين النسق الشامي هي الأغنام، والبقعة كلها الروضة، وأصغر النجوم النَّقَد وهي صغار الغنم.

stories.title: الراعي في الروضة
stories.text: رأى العرب بين الجاثي والحوّاء مرعًى مسيّجًا: سطران طويلان من النجوم هما «النسقان» يمتدّان إلى المجرة كالسياجين، أحدهما شامي والآخر يماني. قال ابن قتيبة: «وفي وسط النسقين كوكب يقال له الراعي، ويقال لما بين النسقين الروضة». فالراعي واقف وكلبه بجانبه، وغنمه ترعى بين النجوم الخافتة داخل السياج، والضباع والذئاب تحوم في الظلام خارجه. وهو من أتمّ المشاهد في سماء العرب.

greek.seen: Asclepius, the healer, holding a great snake.

stories.title: The healer who cheated death
stories.text: Asclepius, son of Apollo, was taught medicine by the centaur Chiron and became so skilled that he could bring the dead back to life. Hades complained that the underworld was emptying, so Zeus struck Asclepius with a thunderbolt. Then, to honour his gift, Zeus placed him among the stars holding a serpent, the symbol of healing that still appears on medical signs today.
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: أسكليبيوس الطبيب يمسك ثعبانًا عظيمًا.

stories.title: الطبيب الذي غلب الموت
stories.text: تعلّم أسكليبيوس ابن أبولو الطبّ على يد القنطور خيرون، فبلغ من البراعة أن صار يحيي الموتى. فشكا هاديس من أن العالم السفلي يخلو، فضرب زيوس أسكليبيوس بصاعقة، ثم كرّم موهبته فرفعه بين النجوم ممسكًا بثعبان، رمز الشفاء الذي ما زال يظهر على شعارات الطب إلى اليوم.

arab.seen: Sagitta, the Arrow: a few small, faint stars on the edge of the Milky Way, "whose light has a darkness and dullness in it". The poet states plainly that the Arabs gave it no name.

full.e: After them come the stars of the Arrow, and the Bedouins gave it no known name;
they are, you should know, small stars that the eyes almost fail to see,
with a darkness and dullness in their light; they lie at the edge of the Milky Way.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 3 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: السهم: نجوم صغار خافتة على حافة المجرة «في نورهن ظلمة وكُدرة». ويقول الناظم صراحة إن الأعراب لم تسمّه باسم معروف.

greek.seen: An arrow.

stories.title: Whose arrow?
stories.text: Several stories claim this arrow. It may be the arrow Heracles used to shoot the eagle that tore at Prometheus's liver every day. It may be the arrow Apollo used to kill the Cyclopes. Or it may be Cupid's (Eros's) arrow. It sits between the Eagle and the Swan.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia

ar.seen: سهم.

stories.title: سهم من؟
stories.text: يدّعي هذا السهم أكثر من حكاية: قد يكون السهم الذي رمى به هرقل النسر الذي كان ينهش كبد بروميثيوس كل يوم، أو السهم الذي قتل به أبولو العمالقة ذوي العين الواحدة، أو سهم إيروس (كيوبيد). ويقع بين العقاب والدجاجة.

arab.seen: Aquila, the Eagle, which the Bedouins call al-Nasr al-Ta'ir, "the flying eagle". Its bright star Altair has one star in front and one behind, its two outspread wings. Nearby stars outside the figure are al-Zilman, the young male ostriches.

stories.title: The eagle in flight
stories.text: Ibn Qutayba writes: "The Flying Eagle faces the Falling one, with the Milky Way between them. It is a bright star between two stars on either side, three in a line; it is said the two stars are its wings, which it has spread." The two great birds face each other across the river of light: one folding its wings to drop, the other soaring. The modern name Altair comes from al-Ta'ir, "the flyer".
stories.source: Ibn Qutayba, Kitab al-Anwa' (9th c.)

full.e: It is followed by the stars of the Eagle, which the Bedouins call
its Flying Eagle: stars, some shining and some dim.
Among them is a star of dazzling light, the one called the Flying Eagle;
one star follows it and one star goes before it: those are its two wings, as we know.
It is followed by many stars lying outside this figure,
close to the Eagle: the Bedouins know them as al-Zilman, the young male ostriches.

poem.by: Ibn al-Sufi, Urjuzat al-Kawakib (around 1000 CE), all 6 couplets for this constellation

ar.seen: العقاب، وتسمّيه الأعراب النسر الطائر. نجمه النيّر بين نجمين أحدهما أمامه والآخر خلفه هما جناحاه المبسوطان. ونجوم قريبة خارج الصورة هي الظِّلمان، أي ذكور النعام.

stories.title: النسر في طيرانه
stories.text: قال ابن قتيبة: «وأما الطائر فهو إزاء الواقع وبينهما المجرة، وهو كوكب منير بين كوكبين عن جانبيه، فهي ثلاثة مصطفّة، يقال إن الكوكبين جناحاه قد بسطهما». فالطائران العظيمان يتقابلان على نهر النور، أحدهما يضمّ جناحيه لينقضّ والآخر يحلّق. واسم Altair الحديث من «الطائر».

greek.seen: The eagle of Zeus.

stories.title: Zeus's eagle and Ganymede
stories.text: The eagle was Zeus's own bird, which carried his thunderbolts. In the most famous story Zeus sent it, or became it himself, to carry off Ganymede, a beautiful Trojan prince, to Mount Olympus to be the cup-bearer of the gods. Nearby Aquarius is sometimes said to be Ganymede, pouring from his jar.
stories.source: Pseudo-Eratosthenes, Catasterismi; Hyginus, De Astronomia; Ovid, Metamorphoses 10

ar.seen: نسر زيوس.

stories.title: نسر زيوس وغانيميد
stories.text: كان النسر طائر زيوس الذي يحمل صواعقه. وفي أشهر حكاية أرسله زيوس، أو صار هو نفسه نسرًا، ليختطف غانيميد الأمير الطروادي الجميل إلى جبل الأولمب ليكون ساقي الآلهة. ويقال إن ساكب الماء القريب منه هو غانيميد يسكب من جرّته.

china.seen: Niulang, the Cowherd (Altair), carrying his two children.

stories.title: The Cowherd
stories.text: Altair is Niulang, the cowherd who married the Weaver Girl. The two faint stars on either side are said to be their two children, whom he carries in baskets on a shoulder pole as he chases his wife across the sky. Only on Qixi, when the magpies build their bridge across the Milky Way, can the family be together.
stories.source: Traditional; Wikipedia, 'The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl'

ar.seen: نيولانغ، راعي البقر (النسر الطائر)، يحمل طفليه.

stories.title: راعي البقر
stories.text: النسر الطائر هو نيولانغ راعي البقر الذي تزوّج فتاة النسيج. ويقال إن النجمين الخافتين على جانبيه طفلاهما، يحملهما في سلّتين على عصا على كتفه وهو يطارد زوجته عبر السماء. ولا تجتمع الأسرة إلا في عيد تشي شي حين تبني طيور العقعق جسرها فوق درب التبانة.

stories.title: The lover across the river
stories.text: Altair is Hikoboshi (Kengyū), the herdsman who loves the weaving princess Orihime. With Vega and Deneb he makes up the Summer Triangle. Sei Shōnagon listed him among her favourite stars (see Taurus).
stories.source: Kitab al-Sama'; Sei Shōnagon, The Pillow Book

ar.seen: هيكوبوشي، الراعي (النسر الطائر).

stories.title: الحبيب على الضفّة الأخرى
stories.text: النسر الطائر هو هيكوبوشي (كينغيو) الراعي الذي يحبّ الأميرة النسّاجة أوريهيمه، وهو مع النسر الواقع وذنب الدجاجة «مثلث الصيف». وقد عدّته سي شوناغون من النجوم التي تحبّها (انظر الثور).

safrica.seen: /Gwi San: Altair is the female steenbok.

stories.title: The female steenbok
stories.text: For the /Gwi San, Altair is the female steenbok, and Vega across the Milky Way is her mate.
stories.source: Astronomical Society of Southern Africa, 'African Ethnoastronomy' (after P. G. Alcock, Venus Rising, 2014)

af.seen: /Gwi San: Altair is die steenbokooi.

stories.title: Die steenbokooi
stories.text: Vir die /Gwi San is Altair die steenbokooi, en Vega oorkant die Melkweg is haar maat.

ar.seen: سان /غوي: النسر الطائر أنثى الستينبوك.

stories.title: أنثى الستينبوك
stories.text: النسر الطائر عند سان /غوي أنثى الستينبوك، والنسر الواقع عبر درب التبانة زوجها.

arab.seen: Delphinus: ten stars, four of them bright. The four bright ones are called Salib al-Ta'ir, "the cross of the Flyer" (the flying eagle), and the Arabs also call them al-Qa'ud, a young riding camel. A small, bright star beneath is 'Amud al-Salib, "the pillar of the cross", at the base of the dolphin's tail.

stories.title: The young camel
stories.text: The little diamond of Delphinus is al-Qa'ud to the Arabs: a young camel just old enough to be ridden, standing near the flying eagle. This is a name and a picture rather than a told story, part of the way the Bedouin filled their sky with the animals of their own life.
stories.source: Commentary on the site (Abha al-Mawakib)

full.e: After it, the Dolphin: stars that all rise when the Eagle appears;
ten in number, gathered together, four of them shining.
These four bright ones are all known and famous;
they shine in the dark for those who gaze, and they are called the Cross of the Flyer,
and the Arabs may call them the Young Camel: so the reporters tell in their books.
Beneath the Young Camel is a small star, but one with a bright lustre;
